title: DialogueDown conformance fixture
description: One case from the conformance corpus. A fixture states what a runtime must do with a playbook: either the verdict a reader must reach about the document, or the conversation a runner must be able to hold with it. Fixtures are hand-authored from the design rather than recorded from a run, so unknown properties are refused: a misspelled field here is a mistake to surface, not a newer writer talking to an older reader.

oneOf.title: A readable fixture
oneOf.description: Asks whether a reader can load the document at all.

oneOf.title: A playable fixture
oneOf.description: Asks whether a runner holds the same conversation.

$schema.description: Where an editor can find this schema.

name.description: What this fixture asserts, as a sentence a failure can report.

playbook.description: The document this fixture is about, named relative to the fixture. Named rather than assumed, so a case may point at a document under any name.

because.description: Why the fixture claims what it claims, for a human reviewing the corpus. Required: a case nobody can weigh on sight is a case that silently rots.

verdict.description: What a reader must do with the document. A refusal's message is never asserted, so that every runtime may explain itself in its own language.

session.description: One conversation: what a driver sends, interleaved with what the runtime must reply, in the order it happens.

send.description: One message from the driver, in the protocol's own vocabulary.

oneOf.description: Proceed past what was just said, or ask where the run stands.

choose.description: The zero-based position, among the options just offered, of the one taken.

supply.description: What the world says, by the key the runtime asked about.

start.description: The anchor to begin at, instead of the playbook's entry.

expect.description: One message the runtime must produce next. No entry carries a node reference: a reference is a position, and an assertion that changed whenever the compiler renumbered would be a liability rather than a test.

speaker.description: The speaker's name, never their index. Absent for the anonymous default speaker, who has no name.

asked.description: The options offered, in the order offered. What was taken is not recorded here: the next send says so.

available.description: Whether the option may be taken. A failing option is shown unavailable rather than hidden.

performed.description: The effect, as the playbook names it. Left loose until the runtime settles the shape.

resolve.description: The keys the runtime asked the world about.

invalidated.description: An offered option that stopped being available. Left loose until the runtime settles the shape.

at.description: Where the run stands, in reply to describe. Left loose until the runtime settles the shape.

out.description: What leads onward from there, in reply to describe. Left loose until the runtime settles the shape.

speech.description: What was said, or an option's label. An array asserts the playbook's own fragments, exactly as it serializes them; a plain string asserts the flattening of those fragments -- a deliberately weaker claim, chosen so a fixture that is not about styling stays readable. See playbook-0.schema.json for what a fragment is.

oneOf.description: Every fragment's plain text, concatenated, with style markers dropped and resolved queries substituted.
